wsp104_decision.conclusion: A shell-owned discovery selector can fit the present namespace contract if canonicalization completes before any tenant landing render or context publication. An alias is not a new FoundUp identity, tenant-owned family or app route.
wsp104_decision.basis: WSP104 gives the shell /f/ management and discovery, while each tenant owns one canonical /f/{foundup_id} family. Keep the canonical visible path and internal identity at the entry boundary.
wsp104_decision.interpretation_limit: This is a qualified interpretation of existing ownership/invariants, not an explicit alias clause already implemented in WSP104. Record the selector-versus-tenant-family distinction in the existing contract docs; no protocol weakening or external runtime authority is required. Rendering and retaining /f/amibot as an alternate tenant entry is not the selected design.

representation.shape: One optional nonempty lowercase ASCII slug string matching ^[a-z0-9_]+$; omission means no alias. Reject explicit empty/null/non-string, whitespace, separators, percent syntax and uppercase rather than coercing or case-folding.
representation.no_inference: Never infer from display_name, public_url_or_route, prose or a manifest prefix. No alias array, separate module, standalone alias file or duplicate entity is required.
representation.data_boundary: Do not add this field to current production registry records or regenerate a changed catalog in this capability slice. Synthetic fixtures exercise presence; absent current fields preserve bytes and behavior.

validation_contract: Projector owns alias reservation validation over every registry entity BEFORE portfolio filtering: reject malformed aliases, duplicate aliases and any collision with any canonical foundup_id, including self, hidden and non-eligible entries. Do not resolve collisions by order or first match.

Alias emission requires BOTH existing portfolio eligibility and explicit public_surface_status in discoverable/listed/promoted. Hidden or missing/unknown visibility suppresses alias emission while leaving the old canonical entity eligibility rules unchanged.

Keep projection validation independently fail-closed: reject injected/non-derived aliases and alias drift. Reuse a small alias-validation helper from generation and validation rather than duplicating rules; preserve existing ValidationReport API.

Public sanitizer admits only the new explicit field. Shell rejects malformed/ambiguous aliases and visible alias/canonical collisions before lookup; full-registry hidden collision assurance remains the projector validation responsibility, not a fabricated browser guarantee.
shell_contract: Preserve the existing app/app-deep-link branch BEFORE any catalog fetch. Alias /app requests get that same member handoff; do not add app alias resolution, app mounting or storage/runtime scopes.

Alias lookup is available only for exact /f/{alias} with optional one trailing slash. Reject alias /other and other deeper paths; do not reinterpret legacy canonical deep-path behavior as part of this change.

Use exactly one URL-segment decode, retaining current canonical behavior; malformed percent input and decoded slash/backslash/percent/non-slug tokens must never reach alias render. Double-encoded separator must not be decoded a second time.

Resolve exactly one eligible projected alias to its canonical item. Before renderEntry or populateConciergeContext, call history.replaceState with a constructed same-origin /f/{canonical foundup_id} path and set the local foundupId to that canonical ID. Never take a replacement URL from data. Alias canonicalization drops query/hash rather than using them as identity inputs; canonical no-alias requests keep existing behavior.

If history canonicalization is unavailable or throws, stop landing render/context publication and show the existing failure/not-found surface. No shared-ID fallback and no alias under canonical labeling.

Keep current canonical routes free of automatic /member/foundup.html redirects. Existing no-location.replace assertions are not behavioral proof: explicitly test canonical no-op versus alias history replacement, ordering and failure. Do not merely evade a source-string assertion.
